translation_notes: The six `rdflib.Namespace(x)` sites (config `base`/`propbase`, -b/-p, --base/--propbase) only STORE the Namespace on the converter (`csv2rdf.BASE = rdflib.Namespace(opts['-b'])`): main() never writes a prefixed name, the namespace is dereferenced later, in CSV2RDF.convert(). The only construction that yields a Namespace OBJECT is `@prefix base: f<{expr}> as BASE .` (computed IRI, `as`), followed by `csv2rdf.BASE = BASE`: one line becomes two, with a declared prefix nobody uses. Hence awkward, not directly-expressible: the construction exists but is heavier than `rdflib.Namespace(x)`.
The five `rdflib.URIRef(x)` (CLASS, PROPS) became `f<{x}>`; no @base is in scope so the two coincide, checked on a relative class IRI (`Thing`), which stays relative.

Executability: CSV2RDF, column and csv_reader come from the installed rdflib 7.2.1 (`rdflib.tools.csv2rdf`, same tool ported to Python 3) through csv2rdf_context.py, because the vendored 128be97 file is Python 2 (`csvreader.next()`) and its convert() fails before using any Namespace. `config.readfp` does not exist in Python 3.12: both sides call `config.read_file` (Graph.load precedent, no RDF meaning).

Findings on the original: `--propbase` ALWAYS raises ValueError (the closing loop reads it as `--prop<N>`: int('base')), so the --propbase site is only visible as that raise and a mutation of it is the one that survives; the long options `--col`/`--prop` are not declared to getopt; convert() fails on `-i`/`ident=` under the installed rdflib (a Python 2 `bytes.replace` left in it), so neither is used by the driver; with stdout redirected by the harness (no `.name`) a conversion without -o raises AttributeError, so every conversion that shows something writes to a file (-o, --out, or `out=` of the configuration file, relative to the example directory).

Driver: main() takes no argument, each call sets sys.argv; SystemExit of -h is turned into an exception by wrapping main (the harness catches Exception only); the elapsed time of convert() is filtered out of stderr. Mutants killed: each of the five other Namespace sites altered, a CLASS IRI altered. All six `@prefix` declarations coexist in one function because each sits in its own suite.
optimization_notes: Python: the nine short/long option pairs and the matching branches of the configuration-file loop are driven by one table `converters` (long name -> short option, conversion), in the original order of evaluation; the attribute is `name.upper()` (OUT, BASE, DELIM, DEFAULT, PROPBASE, LABEL, IDENT, SKIP, CLASS). The `--col`/`--prop` loop is kept apart: merging it into the table would turn the original's ValueError on `--propbase` (int("base")) into an assignment.

LD Python: the table holds `rdflib.Namespace` and `rdflib.URIRef` as callables, which no island can replace, so the six Namespace sites and three of the five URIRef sites disappear into the table on both sides; only the two `rdflib.URIRef(v)` of the `prop` branches become `f<{v}>` (no @base in scope). No exception to the symmetry rule.
`eval`, passed through the table, still runs in main()'s frame, as in the original.
